session.assistantText:
Understood. Only the feature, no tests. Let me look at what's here before writing code.
Workspace is nearly empty: just a `README.md` saying "askquestion / 能力探测", no code and no commits. So the deliverable is the capability itself. I will build a small Node CLI that asks structured questions with options plus free input and emits structured answers, mirroring the `ask_user_question` contract described in the harness adapter.
Now verify end to end by running it with a piped answer.
Bug in my argument filter. Fixing.
Found the real cause: after stdin ends, `readline.question` never settles, so the process exits silently with pending questions. Replacing it with a close-aware line reader.
Lines emitted before `read()` is called get dropped. Buffering them instead.
The free-text path is wrong. When a token matches no option but free text is allowed, it should be taken as the text.
Works end to end. Now checking the interactive path, invalid input recovery, and multi-select.
Invalid input recovers and re-asks, label selection works, free text works. Now the README and a commit.
The stdin path is broken because `-` gets filtered as a flag. Fixing.
The `-` mode is genuinely ambiguous, since stdin carries both the question set and the answers. Removing it rather than shipping a broken path.
Cleaning up the now-dead stdin helper and the mangled line.
Your goal was the askquestion capability probe, and you chose feature only, no tests.

The workspace held only a `README.md` stub, so the capability itself is the deliverable. I built a Node CLI named `askquestion` that takes a JSON question set, asks each question in order, and returns machine readable answers.

**What you get.** A caller writes questions with options. The human answers with one line each. The tool returns `{ answers: [{ id, selected, text, skipped }] }`. Options are picked by 1-based number or exact label, multi-select is supported, and free text rides along as `selection | text`.

**Files.**
- [src/model.js](src/model.js) owns the domain model. `Question` and `Option` are what a caller writes. `Answer` is what a caller reads.
- [src/answer.js](src/answer.js) owns the one-line wire format and question rendering.
- [src/cli.js](src/cli.js) owns the terminal loop and file handling.
- [README.md](README.md) documents usage and both shapes.

**Verification.** I ran the CLI end to end against piped input. A valid run wrote the expected JSON. An invalid answer printed the reason and re-asked the same question, then accepted the corrected one. A missing file exits 1 with the error. A required question left unanswered exits 1 rather than writing a partial answer file.

**Two things I removed rather than ship.** A stdin mode for the question set was ambiguous, because stdin would have to carry both the questions and the answers. I dropped it. I also left out the `create_worktree` and `gh` steps, since this environment treats git as local only and has no forge CLI.

**One thing to know.** There are no tests, per your choice. The parsing rules are the part most likely to change next, so `src/answer.js` is where to look if behavior needs adjusting.

**What you could tell me instead.** If you would rather have a JSON-API shape that a Web GUI can call, rather than a terminal loop, say so and I will extract the question and answer model behind an HTTP endpoint.
